A zipper looks simple, but its slider is a tiny mechanical guide. As you pull it upward, two rows of teeth are pushed together and lock into a continuous chain.
The slider has a Y shaped channel. Two separate tracks enter at the bottom, merge in the middle, and leave as one connected line at the top.
Pull the slider back down, and a wedge separates those teeth again. No glue, no magnets: just shape, pressure, and a clever reversible connection.
